name: Gokyo Lakes and Gokyo Ri
why: The quieter valley west of Everest: a chain of turquoise glacier lakes beside the Ngozumpa, the longest glacier of Nepal, and four 8,000 m peaks from the top of Gokyo Ri.
book: Sagarmatha National Park permit and the Khumbu municipality permit. Fly to Lukla. Teahouses at every stop.
water: Boiled water from the teahouses; treat stream water.
dangers: Altitude: sleep at Dole and Machhermo before Gokyo (4,790 m), never more than 500 m higher a night.
Headache or breathlessness at rest: go down.
turnaround: Start up Gokyo Ri before sunrise and be down by 11:00, before the clouds come up.

points.name: Lukla
points.note: The mountain airstrip where you land from Kathmandu.

points.name: Namche Bazaar
points.note: Two nights in the Sherpa capital to get used to the height.

points.name: Machhermo
points.note: A small yak-herding settlement at 4,470 m, last night before the lakes.

points.name: Gokyo
points.note: Lodges on the shore of the third lake, Dudh Pokhari, beside the moraine of the Ngozumpa Glacier.

points.name: Gokyo Ri
points.note: A 5,357 m hill above the lake: Everest, Lhotse, Makalu and Cho Oyu in one view.
